title: Much of the delay occurs before formal referral, in proponent studies a statutory clock would not cover
oneLiner: The clock can only time the part of the process it can see.
body: Proponents often spend years on baseline surveys, consultation and design changes before a project is formally referred. A statutory deadline starts at referral and would leave that period untouched, so headline approval times could fall without total project timelines changing much.
contextBackground: Timing data on the pre-referral phase is thin because it is not recorded anywhere official; the claim rests on proponents' own accounts and on inquiry evidence rather than a systematic dataset.
contextDisagreement: The claim is plausible and weakly evidenced. Supporters of deadlines answer that much pre-referral work is itself driven by uncertainty about what the regulator will require, which clearer standards and deadlines would reduce.

evidenceItems.citation: Productivity Commission, Resources Sector Regulation, study report, 2020 — evidence on pre-referral timelines

otherClaim.title: The 2025 overhaul of national environment law will deliver faster approvals without weakening protection

claimItself.title: The 2025 overhaul of national environment law will deliver faster approvals without weakening protection
claimItself.oneLiner: The reforms have passed. Whether they do both of the things promised is the question as they roll out through 2026.
claimItself.body: The Environment Protection Reform Act passed on 28 November 2025 after a Labor–Greens deal, creating a National Environmental Protection Agency, national environmental standards, a streamlined assessment pathway and a ministerial national-interest exemption. Fossil fuel projects are excluded from the fast track and the exemption. The EPA began on 1 July 2026; the faster assessment provisions commence by 1 December 2026.

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: The reforms leave the minister, not the national environmental standards, as the final decision-maker for high-impact projects

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: The streamlined pathway, bioregional plans and the national-interest exemption could let large-scale land clearing, critical-minerals mines and badly sited renewable projects through with less scrutiny than before

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: Coal, gas and petroleum projects should be excluded from the streamlined approval pathway and the national-interest exemption

usedIn.relationSentence: This claim contradicts “The 2025 overhaul of national environment law will deliver faster approvals without weakening protection”

strengthDefinitions.decisive: It defeats the parent claim if accepted.
strengthDefinitions.relevant: It counts against the parent claim without settling it.
strengthDefinitions.tangential: True perhaps, but it does not land against this claim.
